gold_answers.q01: Hoerl and Kennard introduced the theory in 1970.
gold_answers.q04: The sample is randomly partitioned into k equal-sized folds; one fold is kept as validation data and the other k-1 folds are used for training.
gold_answers.q08: The design matrix has less than full rank, so the moment matrix cannot be inverted and the system has infinitely many solutions.
gold_answers.q18: The lasso tends to select one variable from the group and ignore the others; the elastic net has a grouping effect that gives correlated features equal weights.
gold_answers.q20: The holdout method assigns data to one training and one test set and runs once; k-fold cross-validation rotates through k folds and averages multiple runs.
gold_answers.q09: Ridge regression, introduced by Hoerl and Kennard in 1970.
gold_answers.q10: Robert Tibshirani popularised the lasso in 1996.
gold_answers.q16: The overfitting article lists model comparison, cross-validation, regularization, early stopping, pruning, Bayesian priors and dropout; the decision tree article says pruning is necessary for trees.
